title: WPMS/520/2016 of MANAGING DIRECTOR Vs SMT. BHAGWATI BISHT-1

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
WRIT PETITION (S/S) NO. 1327 OF 2007
Kamla Negi and others
.........Petitioners
Vs.
State of Uttarakhand and others

.......Respondents
Present:
Mr. Pradeep Chamiyal, Advocate for the petitioners.
Mr. P.C. Bisht, Add. C.S.C. for the State/respondent nos. 1 & 2.
Mr. Sandeep Kothari, Advocate for respondent no. 3.
Mr. Gopal K. Verma, Advocate for respondent no. 4.
Mr. Alok Mahra, Advocate for respondent no. 5.
WRIT PETITION (M/S) NO. 520 OF 2016
Managing Director, Kumaon Mandal Vikas Nigam Ltd.
.........Petitioner
Vs.
Smt. Bhagwati Bisht-1 and others
 .......Respondents
Present:
Mr. Sandeep Kothari, Advocate for the petitioner and proforma respondent nos.
60 and 61.
Mr. Lalit Belwal, Advocate for the private respondents.
Mr. Alok Mahra, Advocate for respondent no. 59.
Hon'ble Ravindra Maithani, J. (Oral)
Since common questions of law and facts are involved in
both the petitions, they are being decided by this common judgment.
2. Petitioners in WPSS No. 1327 of 2007 and the private
respondents in WPMS No. 520 of 2016 were employees of U.P.
Digital Limited, Bhowali, a Unit manufacturing wrist watches (for
short, "the Unit"). The Unit was earlier a subsidiary company of Uttar
Pradesh Industrial Development Corporation (" the UPSIDC"), but on
20.04.2000, the Unit was handed over to Kumaon Mandal Vikas
Nigam Ltd. (for short, "the KMVN Ltd."). The Unit was not

2
performing well. It was running in losses. Therefore, a decision was
taken for offering voluntary retirement to its workers. Accordingly, the
petitioners in WPSS No. 1327 of 2007 and the private respondents in
WPMS No. 520 of 2016 took voluntary retirement under the Voluntary
Retirement Scheme, on 31.05.2000 (the petitioner in WPSS No. 1327
of 2007 and the private respondents in WPMS No. 520 of 2016 shall
hereinafter be referred to as "the claimants").
3. It may be noted here that earlier the workmen in the Unit
were not paid dearness allowances. A settlement took place between
the management and the workmen in the year 1982 and 1994, which
were registered as Settlement No. 05 of 1982 and Settlement No. 03 of
1995, respectively. But, after 1994, the dearness allowances were not
paid to the workmen; it was freezed. When on 31.05.2000, the
claimants took voluntary retirement, they were assured that the amount
of freezed DA would be paid to them. But, it was not paid. Therefore,
WPSS No. 1327 of 2007 has been filed by the petitioners claiming the
arrears of freezed DA.
4. Some of the private respondents in WPMS No. 520 of
2016 also approached this Court, but in view of availability of
alternate remedy, they subsequently approached the Industrial Tribunal
and Labour Court, Haldwani, Nainital (for short, "the Labour Court")
and filed a claim under Section 33C (2) of the Uttar Pradesh Industrial
Disputes Act, 1947 (hereinafter referred to as the "Act"). The Labour
Court by its order dated 30.07.2015 upheld the claims of the private
respondents in WPMS No. 520 of 2016 and directed the KMVN Ltd.

3
to make payment to the private respondents in WPMS No. 520 of
2016. The order dated 30.07.2015 passed by the Labour Court is
impugned in WPMS No. 520 of 2016.
WPMS No. 520 of 2016
5. The impugned order dated 30.07.2015 has been
challenged, inter alia, on the ground that :-
(i) The Unit was transferred to the KMVN Ltd. after
creation of the State of Uttarakhand.
(ii) The State of Uttarakhand had not been made a
party before the Labour Court.
(iii) The claim under Section 33C(2) of the Act is not
maintainable.
(iv) There has been no agreement between the KMVN
Ltd. and the Unit, on the basis of which it may be
said that the KMVN Ltd. is liable to pay any dues.
(v) The claim of the workmen relates to the period
prior to creation of the State of Uttarakhand.
6. The private respondents have denied the averments made
by the KMVN Ltd. According to the counter affidavit filed by the
private respondents, the Unit was transferred to the KMVN Ltd. on
20.04.2000, which was much prior to the creation of State of
Uttarakhand and the private respondents had retired on 31.05.2000,
which was also prior to the creation of the State of Uttarakhand. The
KMVN Ltd. is liable to pay the dues of the workmen. The KMVN Ltd.
has stepped into the shoes of the UPSIDC. The KMVN Ltd. in various

4
communications of it, beginning from 01.11.2002 till 23.07.2007
acknowledged the claim of the workmen.
7. On behalf of respondent no. 59, the UPSIDC, counter
affidavit is filed and it is averred that the UPSIDC has nothing to do
with the matter as the Unit had already been transferred to the KMVN
Ltd. on 20.04.2000.
WPSS No. 1327 of 2007
8. The petitioners' claim is based on admission. It is the case
of the petitioners that the KMVN Ltd. has throughout admitted the
claim of the petitioners and, in fact, also acknowledged that the
voluntary retirement was taken by the workmen on the assurance given
by the KMVN Ltd. that the arrears of freezed DA would be paid to
them as and when budget is received from the State.
9. State has filed its counter affidavit. Mainly, it is objected
to on the following grounds:-
(i) The claim is made after seven years, which is not
maintainable.
(ii) State of Uttarakhand has no liability because the
petitioners retired from service on 31.05.2000
pursuant to Government Order dated 05.10.2000 of
the State of Uttar Pradesh.
10. Respondent no.3 the KMVN Ltd. filed counter affidavit.
It is averred by the KMVN Ltd. that the KMVN had merely sent a

5
proposal to the State Government for payment of dues of voluntary
retired 80 employees but the Government had declined the proposal on
13.09.2007. The KMVN Ltd. have objected to the claim on the ground
that no legal ground, or legally enforceable right has been placed and
taken in the writ petition, hence the petitioner deserves to be rejected.
11. Respondent no. 5, the UPSIDC also filed separate counter
affidavit and denied its liability.
12. Heard the learned counsel for the parties and perused the
record.
13. One and the same claim has been preferred before this
Court in WPSS No. 1327 of 2007 and before the Labour Court under
Section 33(2) of the Act. By the impugned order dated 30.07.2015, the
Labour Court found that there were settlements between the workmen
and the management on 30.12.1982 and 11.11.1994, which were to be
respected even beyond three years in view of settled legal position.
The Labour Court also recorded that the claims of the workmen had
been admitted by the KMVN Ltd. and accordingly, upheld the claim
and directed the KMVN Ltd. to honour the claim of the workmen.
14. Learned counsel for the KMVN Ltd. would submit that
when the Unit was transferred to the KMVN Ltd., it was a sick Unit.
The KMVN Ltd. was merely a nodal agency to execute the voluntary
retirement scheme. He would submit the following arguments as well:-

6
(i) The KMVN Ltd. received representations from the
workmen, which were forwarded to the State
Government, but finally the claims were declined
on 13.09.2007 by the State Government.
(ii) Since the State of Uttarakhand had already turned
down the claim of the workmen on 13.09.2017, the
liability cannot be said to be admitted liability and
in view of it, the claim under Section 33C(2) of the
Act cannot be held maintainable.
(iii) The impugned order directs the KMVN Ltd. to
make the payment and to receive it from the State
of Uttarakhand, but the State of Uttarakhand had
not been made a party before the Labour Court.
15. On the other hand, learned counsel for the private
respondents in WPMS No. 520 of 2016 would submit that whatever
has been argued before this Court, none of such objections were ever
taken before the Labour Court. It is submitted that what was due to the
workmen was admitted to the KMVN Ltd. because the details were
furnished by the KMVN Ltd. itself as recorded in the impugned order
dated 30.07.2015 of the Labour Court. Learned counsel would also
argue that even if the State of Uttarakhand denies the liability to pay
the dues of the workmen, the KMVN Ltd., the principal employer
cannot absolve of its liability, which it agreed when the claimants
opted for their retirement. It is argued that the liability was admitted
and the claim was rightly entertained under Section 33C(2) of the Act.

7
16. Learned counsel for the petitioners in WPSS No. 1327 of
2007 would submit that the liability is admitted. The petitioners had
opted for voluntary retirement on the condition that the arrears of
freezed DA would be paid to then after retirement. The Unit is a
subsidiary of the KMVN Ltd., which was transferred to it in the year
2000.
17. Learned State Counsel would submit that the State of
Uttarakhand has no role in it. The KMVN Ltd. is an autonomous body.
The principal employer is the KMVN Ltd., who has its own resources
and funds, therefore, the KMVN Ltd. is liable to pay the dues and not
the State of Uttarakhand.
18. The factual position is not much in dispute.
19. In WPSS No. 1327 of 2007, the State of Uttarakhand in
its counter affidavit has taken a plea of laches stating herein that after
seven years, the writ petition is not maintainable. Undoubtedly, delay
and laches also plays a significant role while deciding any writ
petition. As such, there is no limitation prescribed, but as a general rule
in suits for recovery of arrears etc. the general principle of civil law
should be taken into consideration.
20. The claim was made before the Labour Court some time
in the year 2003 and the impugned order dated 30.07.2015 records that
before that a Writ Petition No. 788 of 2001 had been filed before this
Court. It was withdrawn and thereafter the claim was filed before the
labour court.

8
21. The claimants took voluntary retirement on 31.05.2000.
Generally, such claim should be raised within a period of three years.
In the impugned order dated 30.07.2015, reference has been made to
two settlements between the management and the workmen, and
finding has been recorded based on principle of law that the settlement
remains in force until replaced by another settlement, which was never
done. In fact, the freezed DA in the year 1994 was a kind of recurring
liability till 31.05.2000, when the claimants retired voluntarily. It had
become due on that day. Thereafter it was not recurred.
22. In their counter affidavit filed in WPMS No. 520 of 2016,
the private respondents in para 9 had given the list of communications,
which the KMVN Ltd. had made to the State Government admitting
the liability and first of such communication is dated 01.11.2002.
There is another communication and, in fact, in that communication,
which is Annexure 3 to the counter affidavit filed on behalf of the
private respondents in WPMS No. 520 of 2016, details of dues of
employees have been given and at Sr. No. 5 of it what is stated is
"payment of arrears of VRS compensation due to hike of DA to VRS
employees". Not only this, thereafter on 06.09.2003, 13.10.2003,
25.05.2006 and many more communications were made. These
communications were made by the KMVN Ltd. seeking budgets for
payment of arrears of DA to the claimants. It may be noted at the cost
of repetition that the claimants took voluntary retirement when they
were under the employment of the KMVN Ltd. These communications

9
of the KMVN Ltd., in fact, are admission on the claim of the
petitioners.
23. WPSS No. 1327 of 2007 was filed in the year 2007. As
state, the KMVN had been regularly acknowledging it's liability right
for 01.11.2002 till 25.05.2006. Till then, regularly the KMVN Ltd. had
been acknowledging the liability. There is no question of laches or
delay. As stated, the claim was made before the Labour Court in the
year 2003 itself. There also is no laches. Hence, it cannot be said that
WPSS No. 1327 of 2007 is bad for reason of delay or laches.
24. There is another argument with regard to maintainability
of claim under Section 33C(2). Section 33C(2) of the Act is as
hereunder:-
"33C. Recovery of money due from an
employer. - (1).....................
2. Where any workman is entitled to receive
from the employer any money or any benefit which is
capable of being computed in terms of money and if any
question arises as to the amount of money due or as to the
amount at which such benefit should be computed, then the
question may, subject to any rules that may be made under
this Act, be decided by such Labour Court as may be
specified in this behalf by the appropriate Government
within a period not exceeding three months:
Provided that where the presiding officer of a
Labour Court considers it necessary or expedient so to do,
he may, for reasons to be recorded in writing, extend such
period by such further period as he may think fit."
25. A bare reading of it reveals that it applies to the cases
when the dispute is with regard to computation of amount, which is
due.

10
26. Learned counsel appearing for the KMVN Ltd. would
submit that, in fact, the State of Uttarakhand on 13.09.2007 turned
down the proposal to pay arrears of the freezed DA to the claimed,
therefore, it was not an admitted amount. It was disputed and the
proviso of Section 33 (c) (2) of the Act is not applicable for invoking
claim.
27. This argument has no merit at all. The Unit was earlier a
subsidiary of the UPSIDC. It was not running well. It was handed over
to the KMVN Ltd. on 20.04.2000. It is the date when both the
UPSIDC and the KMVN Ltd. were public sector undertakings in the
State of Uttar Pradesh. The Court would advert to a few more letters at
later stage, but at this stage, it may be noted that repeatedly in its
communications, the KMVN Ltd. had admitted the claim of the
claimants and sought budget from the State of Uttarakhand. The State
of Uttarakhand did not employ these claimants. They were working
with the KMVN Ltd., when they took voluntary retirement. So if there
is a liability to pay any dues to the claimants, it falls on the KMVN
Ltd. It is another issue as to how the KMVN Ltd. manages its funds?
How could it pay? Perhaps this Court need not go on those aspects.
28. Three communications of the KMVN Ltd. are very
important. One, as stated, is a communication dated 01.11.2002, which
is mentioned in the counter affidavit of private respondents in WPMS
No. 520 of 2016, at para 9. This has been made by the incharge
Managing Director of the KMVN Ltd. to the State of Uttarakhand.

11
Along with it, a list of dues has been given, which includes arrears of
dearness allowance. The second communication is communication
dated 02.09.2006 made by the Managing Director of the KMVN Ltd.
to the State of Uttarakhand and the first page bottom lines of this
communication are very significant, which records that till 31.5.20000,
eighty workmen did apply for voluntary retirement scheme, who were
given the benefit of voluntary retirement with the understanding that as
and when the amount of dearness allowance is received from the
Government, it shall be paid to the Government. (It is, Annexure 3 to
the WPSS No. 1327 of 2007). The another communication is dated
23.07.2007, which also records that at the time of accepting the
voluntary retirement, it was agreed between the KMVN Ltd. and the
claimants that the claimants would be paid arrears of dearness
allowance as and when the funds are received from the State
Government.
29. These three and many other communications, which are
referred to in the pleadings of the parties confirm that the KMVN Ltd.
had acknowledged its liability. They were merely seeking funds. The
KMVN Ltd. was the principal employer. Therefore, since the employer
had admitted the liability, a claim under Section 33 C(2) of the Act is
definitely maintainable. It does not become non-maintainable merely
because the State of Uttarakhand on 13.09.2017 declined to release the
finds to the KMVN Ltd. It may be a matter between the KMVN Ltd.
and the State of Uttarakhand. The duty is with the KMVN Ltd. It has
to generate its resources, may it get budget from the State, may it get

12
loan from the State or for any other sources. But, it does not absolve
the KMVN Ltd. of its liability and it does not make the claim under
Section 33C(2) of the Act non-maintainable.
30. In view of the foregoing discussion, the Court is of the
view, the impugned order dated 30.07.2015, in WP (M/S) No. 520 of
2016, does not warrant any interference and WP (M/S) No. 520 of
2016 deserves to be dismissed.
31. The petitioners in WP (S/S) No. 1327 of 2007 are entitled
to the freezed DA. Accordingly the writ petition deserves to be
allowed.
32. The WP (M/S) No. 520 of 2016 is dismissed.
33. The WP (S/S) No. 1327 of 2007 is allowed. The
petitioners in WP (S/S) No. 1327 of 2007 are entitled to freezed DA.
The KMVN Ltd. is directed to make payment of the arrears of freezed
DQA to the petitioner within a period of two months.
